title: Post-Provision Quarantine Policy (Draft) — GPU Fleet Provision-to-Ready
linked_artifacts: Linear: ENG-4823 (GPU health + driver parity gates)
GitHub: redwood/pr-18496 (readiness gate before serving pools)
content:
Status: DRAFT — intended to unblock staged rollout (us-east / A100) while we collect flake data.

Owner: Harish (Infra Fleet Ops)
Primary reviewers: Vanessa (Fleet), Rafael/Miles (SRE), Ethan/Benji (Control Plane), Fiona (SecOps)

---

1) Purpose

Quarantine is the automated safety mechanism that prevents newly provisioned GPU nodes from joining inference-serving pools when we detect high-confidence failures (hardware, driver/toolkit drift, fabric/network issues, or validation agent misconfiguration). This is meant to:
- Protect production serving pools from unstable nodes
- Reduce on-call time spent chasing non-actionable flake (by gating and surfacing failure reasons)
- Make failures “loud” and centralized (Fleet Readiness Service + dashboards) vs. silent partial joins

Non-goals:
- Quarantine is not intended to be a long-term holding state for capacity management. It’s a short-term disposition pending either automatic remediation (re-image/retry) or an operator decision.

---

2) Scope

Applies to:
- Dedicated capacity pools (first priority)
- Shared GPU fleet bring-up in regions where the provision-to-ready automation is enabled

Does not apply to:
- Nodes already in steady-state serving pools (separate health management / draining policies)
- Manual one-off lab clusters

---

3) Definitions

Node readiness states (per ADR-017):
- Allocated: instance exists / reserved; not yet configured
- Provisioning: OS + kube prereqs + agent install in progress
- Validating: running the validation checklist (pre/post-flight checks)
- Ready: passed all required validations and can be added to serving pools
- Quarantined: failed validation(s) beyond allowed retries, or hit a “hard fail” trigger

Quarantine means:
- Node is explicitly marked Quarantined in Fleet Readiness Service
- Node must not be added to serving pools (readiness gate enforced)
- Operator action required OR automated remediation path runs

---

4) Principles

P0 safety > time-to-ready.
- We prefer quarantining a bad node over admitting it and causing production instability.

Actionability.
- If we quarantine, we must provide: reason code, failing step, evidence pointers (logs/artifacts), and recommended next action.

Avoid flip-flopping.
- Quarantine should not oscillate endlessly on flaky validations. Use bounded retries and then quarantine with a clear label (“suspected flake” vs “hard fail”) and escalation path.

Capacity-aware behavior.
- Quarantine should not silently create a large capacity shortfall. When quarantine count spikes, this must surface on dashboards and trigger an operator page/ticket depending on severity.

---

5) Quarantine criteria (what triggers Quarantined)

We classify validation failures into three buckets:
A) Hard Fail (immediate quarantine; no retries)
B) Soft Fail (retry up to N; then quarantine)
C) Flake-prone / Noisy (retry more; if still failing, quarantine but label as “flake-suspected” and create a ticket)

5.1 Hard fail triggers (immediate quarantine)
These indicate a high probability the node is unsafe or misconfigured beyond a transient issue:
- GPU hardware health: persistent ECC errors above threshold, repeated Xid codes in the “blocklist”, missing GPU(s), MIG layout mismatch (if required), inability to initialize NVML
- Driver/toolkit mismatch: NVIDIA driver version differs from expected golden image channel for the pool; CUDA/NCCL mismatch per approved matrix; kernel module load failures
- Security baseline violations: secure boot / kernel params / required packages missing; unauthorized SSH keys present; agent binary signature/provenance check fails
- Kubelet/node identity issues: node joins with wrong labels/taints (e.g., wrong GPU SKU label), wrong cluster CA, or mismatched node/pool identity token
- Validation agent integrity: agent reports tampering, cannot verify configuration source, or is running an unapproved build

Action on hard fail:
- Mark Quarantined immediately
- Cordon + taint (QuarantineNoSchedule)
- If node is already partially joined: drain if any pods scheduled (should be prevented, but assume worst)
- Create a ticket (severity depends on count/impact); see Section 8

5.2 Soft fail triggers (retry then quarantine)
These are likely transient but still unacceptable if persistent:
- Networking throughput below threshold (fabric issues, ENA/NIC config, security group/ACL)
- Storage IOPS or mount checks failing (ephemeral disk not present, wrong RAID config)
- NCCL smoke test fails (timeouts, all-reduce mismatch) but without hardware hard-fail signals
- Runtime smoke test fails (container runtime, CUDA visibility inside container, basic inference canary) without hard-fail indicators
- Node stuck in Validating beyond max duration (watchdog)

5.3 Flake-prone category (retry more; label)
Observed in early rollout (subject to change):
- NCCL smoke test timeouts at low concurrency (likely network jitter)
- Perf canary borderline thresholds during cold start (disk warm-up / image pull)
- Metrics/telemetry emission failure (agent can’t push spans/metrics) when the underlying validation actually passed

NOTE: This category exists to prevent “quarantine storms” from noisy gates. However, the node is still blocked from serving until the gate passes or operator overrides.

---

6) Auto-retry limits and backoff (per step)

This is the default matrix for provision-to-ready v1. Numbers may be adjusted via config without code changes.

Common settings:
- Retry backoff: exponential with jitter
- Max validation wall clock (Validating state): 45 minutes default (fail into quarantine if exceeded)
- Any hard fail: no retry

Step-by-step (defaults):

(1) Preflight: agent heartbeat + config fetch
- Retries: 3
- Backoff: 1m, 2m, 4m
- Quarantine reason if fails: AGENT_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED

(2) GPU discovery + NVML init
- Retries: 0 (hard fail)
- Quarantine reason: GPU_NOT_DETECTED / NVML_INIT_FAILED

(3) GPU health checks (ECC/Xid)
- Retries: 0 (hard fail if above threshold)
- Quarantine reason: GPU_HEALTH_HARD_FAIL
- Thresholds: see Appendix A (needs sign-off)

(4) Driver/CUDA/NCCL parity
- Retries: 0 (hard fail)
- Quarantine reason: DRIVER_PARITY_FAILED

(5) Kubelet join / node Ready (k8s)
- Retries: 5
- Backoff: 30s, 1m, 2m, 4m, 8m
- Quarantine reason: KUBELET_JOIN_FAILED
- Note: if join fails due to cert/identity mismatch, we should treat as hard fail (security) — TBD detectability.

(6) Network validation
- Retries: 3
- Backoff: 2m, 4m, 8m
- Quarantine reason: NETWORK_VALIDATION_FAILED

(7) Storage validation
- Retries: 2
- Backoff: 2m, 6m
- Quarantine reason: STORAGE_VALIDATION_FAILED

(8) NCCL smoke test
- Retries: 4 (flake-prone)
- Backoff: 2m, 4m, 8m, 10m
- Quarantine reason: NCCL_SMOKE_TEST_FAILED (label flake-suspected if timeouts only)

(9) Runtime smoke test (container + CUDA)
- Retries: 2
- Backoff: 2m, 5m
- Quarantine reason: RUNTIME_SMOKE_FAILED

(10) Perf canary (post-provision)
- Retries: 2 (flake-prone)
- Backoff: 5m, 10m
- Quarantine reason: PERF_CANARY_FAILED (label flake-suspected if marginal)

Quarantine on repeated failure:
- For any non-hard-fail step: if max retries exceeded OR validation wall clock exceeded => Quarantined.

---

7) Automated remediation after quarantine

Goal: reduce operator toil for common classes.

Default behavior (v1):
- Auto-reimage once for Soft Fail categories only, if the pool is in “rollout mode” and quarantine rate is below threshold.
- Never auto-reimage on hard fail GPU health signals (risk: hiding true hardware issues).

Proposed remediation decisioning:
- If QUARANTINE_REASON in {NETWORK_VALIDATION_FAILED, STORAGE_VALIDATION_FAILED, RUNTIME_SMOKE_FAILED}: auto-reimage limit = 1
- If QUARANTINE_REASON == NCCL_SMOKE_TEST_FAILED: auto-reimage limit = 0 by default (prefer investigation/tuning); TBD based on data
- If QUARANTINE_REASON == DRIVER_PARITY_FAILED: auto-reimage limit = 0 (this is usually image/channel drift; fix upstream)

After auto-reimage:
- Node returns to Provisioning, then Validating
- If it quarantines again for same reason => stop automation; surface as “repeat quarantine”

Open question:
- If capacity is constrained, should we allow “manual override” to admit a node that only fails perf canary by a small margin? SRE leaning no for Dedicated pools.

---

8) Surfacing quarantined nodes to operators (and customers indirectly)

8.1 Where quarantine shows up

Control plane / Fleet Readiness Service:
- State = Quarantined
- Fields required:
  - quarantine_reason_code (enum)
  - failed_step_name
  - failed_step_attempts
  - first_failure_at, last_failure_at
  - validation_artifacts_uri (logs bundle pointer)
  - image_channel + image_version
  - pool_id, region, gpu_type

Internal Console (ops tooling):
- Quarantined nodes visible in pool detail view
- Filters: reason code, region, gpu type, image version, “repeat quarantine”
- “Suggested action” text derived from reason code

Dashboards:
- Quarantine count by pool/region/GPU
- Quarantine rate (% of allocated nodes)
- Top quarantine reasons (last 24h, 7d)
- Correlation with image channel changes (candidate->stable)

8.2 Notifications / alerting

Default (staged rollout):
- Page SRE/Infra on:
  - Quarantine rate spike above threshold (TBD; initial suggestion: >10% over 30m in a pool with >=20 nodes)
  - Any hard fail GPU health quarantines above small count (e.g., >=3 in 1h) — indicates potential bad batch
- Create ticket (no page) on:
  - Flake-suspected quarantine above threshold (e.g., NCCL timeouts) to drive tuning (ENG-4830 style)

Where:
- #eng-infra + #eng-sre Slack notifications (rollout period)
- PagerDuty: route based on pool ownership (Dedicated primary = Infra on-call; control-plane errors = Platform)

---

9) Operator actions / playbook entrypoints

Primary runbook: Confluence “provision-to-ready failures triage runbook”

Allowed operator actions (in order of safety):
1) Inspect failure reason + artifacts (do not SSH by default)
2) Retry validation (one-click) if classified flake-prone AND within limits
3) Reimage node (preferred over manual mutation)
4) Drain + remove from cluster (if partial join)
5) Manual override to Ready (restricted; see below)

Manual override policy (proposed):
- Only allowed for non-hard-fail reasons AND only during controlled incidents when capacity is critical
- Requires:
  - Approval from Infra EM (Vanessa) or on-call delegate
  - SRE concurrence if node will serve customer traffic
  - Audit event emitted (who/when/why)

---

10) Quarantine reason codes (initial enum)

HARD FAIL:
- GPU_NOT_DETECTED
- NVML_INIT_FAILED
- GPU_HEALTH_HARD_FAIL
- DRIVER_PARITY_FAILED
- SECURITY_BASELINE_FAILED
- NODE_IDENTITY_MISMATCH
- AGENT_INTEGRITY_FAILED

SOFT FAIL:
- KUBELET_JOIN_FAILED
- NETWORK_VALIDATION_FAILED
- STORAGE_VALIDATION_FAILED
- RUNTIME_SMOKE_FAILED

FLAKE-PRONE (still quarantined if persistent):
- NCCL_SMOKE_TEST_FAILED
- PERF_CANARY_FAILED
- TELEMETRY_EMIT_FAILED

Note: We need to ensure the reason code reflects the most actionable “root” failure, not just the last failing step.

---

11) Data retention / forensics

Validation artifacts (logs bundles, summarized outputs) should be retained for at least:
- 14 days for standard
- 30 days for Dedicated pools during rollout (to support customer escalations)

Audit events:
- Quarantine transitions
- Manual overrides
- Image channel/version changes (ties into audit events work)

---

12) Open questions / TODOs

- Thresholds for ECC/Xid: confirm blocklist with Nina + GPU vendor guidance; avoid quarantining harmless transient Xids.
- NCCL smoke test tuning: which failures are truly fabric vs. startup noise? Need to incorporate “retryable” subcodes.
- Auto-reimage rules: SRE concerns about masking systemic image bugs; propose “auto-reimage only if image version unchanged and failure class is infra transient.”
- Capacity shortfall handling: if quarantine removes >X% nodes, do we automatically pause rollout / revert image channel?
- Permissions: who can read quarantine details (logs may contain host identifiers)? Ensure least-privilege (ties to dashboard access request patterns).

---

Appendix A — Draft GPU health thresholds (NOT FINAL)

These are placeholders; do not implement without sign-off:
- ECC: quarantine if any uncorrectable ECC event observed during validation window OR if correctable ECC exceeds rate threshold (TBD)
- Xid: quarantine if Xid in {13, 31, 43, 45, 48, 63, 64, 79, 94, 95, 140} observed in last N minutes (TBD list)

Appendix B — “Stuck in Validating” watchdog

Definition:
- Node enters Validating and does not reach Ready or Quarantined within 45 minutes

Action:
- Transition to Quarantined with reason VALIDATION_TIMEOUT
- Include step it was last attempting + attempt count

(We should confirm this doesn’t fight with long image pulls; perf canary step currently dominates wall clock on cold caches.)
